key_information_units.information: Ambu delivered total organic revenue growth of 8.6% to DKK 1,558m in Q1 2025/26 (reported growth 3.2%), with Endoscopy Solutions as the primary growth engine at 14.4% organic growth.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Revenue increased organically by 8.6% (19.5%) to DKK 1,558m (DKK 1,510m), with reported growth of 3.2% (20.4%). Endoscopy Solutions increased organically by 14.4% (20.6%). Endoscopy Solutions remained Ambu’s primary growth engine in Q1 2025/26, contributing 63% of the total revenue.

key_information_units.information: Within Endoscopy Solutions, Respiratory posted 8.3% organic growth and Urology, ENT, & GI posted 21.0% organic growth, driven by aScope portfolio adoption and new solution momentum.
key_information_units.source_evidence: The Respiratory business group posted 8.3% (17.7%) organic growth... The Urology, ENT, & GI business group posted 21.0% (23.9%) organic growth, mainly driven by the aScope 4 portfolio and continued strong growth momentum for aScope 5 Uretero.

key_information_units.information: Anesthesia & Patient Monitoring posted flat organic growth of -0.1%, reflecting an extraordinarily high revenue baseline from the prior year.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Anesthesia & Patient Monitoring posted flat organic growth of -0.1% (17.8%), reflecting an extraordinarily high revenue achieved in the same quarter last year.

key_information_units.information: EBIT margin before special items was 10.5% (down from 16.1%), negatively impacted by tariff costs and FX headwind; adjusting for these factors, the margin was 15.2%.
key_information_units.source_evidence: EBIT before special items (b.s.i.) was DKK 164m (DKK 243m), with an EBIT margin b.s.i. of 10.5% (16.1%), the latter negatively impacted by tariff costs and FX headwind. Adjusting for tariff costs and FX, Ambu generated an EBIT margin of 15.2% in the quarter.

key_information_units.information: Free cash flow before acquisitions totaled DKK 13m (down from DKK 69m), negatively impacted by elevated net working capital to mitigate geopolitical uncertainties and support growth, plus FX and tariff effects.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Free cash flow (FCF) before acquisitions totaled DKK 13m (DKK 69m). This was mainly negatively impacted by a change in net working capital, which remained elevated to mitigate global geopolitical uncertainties and support growth. FCF was also impacted by both FX headwind and tariff costs.

key_information_units.information: The 2025/26 financial guidance is maintained, with expected organic revenue growth of 10-13% and EBIT margin b.s.i. of 12-14% (14-16% excluding assumed ~2%-pts tariff impacts).
key_information_units.source_evidence: The 2025/26 financial guidance is maintained. ... Organic revenue growth : 10-13% ... EBIT margin b.s.i. : 12-14%[1] 1) 14-16% excluding assumed impacts of ~2%-pts given the current schedule of expected tariffs.

key_information_units.information: Ambu introduced the SureSight Mobile portable video laryngoscope solution, expanding its video laryngoscope portfolio.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Introduction of Ambu’s portable video laryngoscope solution, SureSight Mobile , expanding Ambu’s video laryngoscope portfolio and Respiratory offering. The SureSight Mobile solution features an integrated screen without the need for separate monitors or cables. Its all-in-one design enables clinicians to perform emergent and unplanned intubations swiftly and confidently in demanding environments – whether in an ambulance, emergency room, or remote location – making it a solution targeted for both pre-hospital and hospital settings.

key_information_units.information: Ambu extended the Ambu Recircle Program to include collection and recycling of blades from the SureSight Connect video laryngoscopy solution starting in 2026.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Extension of the Ambu[®] Recircle Program to include the collection and recycling of blades from Ambu’s video laryngoscopy solution, Ambu[®] SureSight Connect, in 2026.

key_information_units.information: Ambu paid DKK 90m in dividend (DKK 0.41 per share) and acquired DKK 38m in treasury shares as part of its share buyback program.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Ambu paid out DKK 90m in dividend in Q1, corresponding to DKK 0.41 per share. In addition, DKK 38m was used to acquire treasury shares in Q1 as part of Ambu’s share buyback program.
